claims.text: A W-based refractory high-entropy alloy with an SCCPs-type microstructure can enhance HER and HOR catalytic activity relative to conventional catalysts.
A W-based refractory high-entropy alloy with an SCCPs-type microstructure can provide greater HER and HOR durability than conventional catalysts.
The as-synthesized W-based refractory HEA has a stable SCCPs microstructure.
The SCCPs microstructure contains coherent delta lamellae and nanoscale precipitates.
A refractory HEA can contain a multielement matrix that includes tungsten.
Tungsten sites and fine-scale lamellar or precipitate features provide active sites for hydrogen adsorption.
The multielement matrix and fine-scale microstructure improve resistance to electrochemically induced structural degradation.
The d-electron configuration of tungsten improves electron-transfer kinetics in HER and HOR.
Synergistic interactions among refractory elements in the HEA improve electron-transfer kinetics.
The SCCPs structure has mechanical stability under tensile deformation.
The SCCPs structure maintains catalytic performance during long-term electrochemical operation.
The SCCPs structure resists dissolution and morphological change in harsh electrochemical environments.
The W-based refractory HEA will exhibit lower HER and HOR overpotentials than Pt-based or monometallic tungsten catalysts.
The W-based refractory HEA will undergo minimal loss of catalytic activity over extended cycling relative to Pt-based or monometallic tungsten catalysts.
Refractory HEAs possess excellent mechanical properties at elevated temperatures.
Tungsten-based HEAs have well-supported thermal robustness.
Direct evidence for electrochemical HER and HOR performance of W-based refractory HEAs is limited.
The optimum alloy composition and surface modification for maximizing HER and HOR activity are unknown.
